event.summary: Removal of legacy tmux stop and attachment paths follows the explicit retirement contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: older tmux terminals are no longer viewable or separately operable through the supervisor after this upgrade; running work in them is deliberately ended during startup. Details: the assigned handlers patch removes foreign-pane ownership probing from Stop (new lines 865-906), all tmux attach setup (1696-1966), and tmux resize operations (2076-2084). Could-be-highest: yes, retiring a running terminal can terminate user-owned processes and discard its screen. Suggested bucket if this were unintended: highest. Confidence: confirmed specification acceptance for this removal; source-only, no execution. proposed_drop: exact specification acceptance, SPEC.md at this commit, Terminal experience, lines 3004-3015: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' The same paragraph explicitly accepts a startup cleanup failure leaving a second agent possible after Restart, and says already-ended agents lose their old screen. SPEC_impl.md lines 2210-2235 explicitly limit the terminal switch points to host runtimes and require grid-only attaches; lines 2236-2238 say every terminal is created in a host. This is not an independent finding about the retired implementation. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources searched. Caveat: this candidate addresses the requested removal contracts, not whether startup retirement correctly implements them; startup retirement is outside this assigned handlers group.

event.summary: Legacy terminal removal can end running work; specification explicitly accepts it
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: after this upgrade, sessions left in old tmux terminals lose their running processes and terminal screens; the supervisor no longer offers the old Stop, attach, or resize paths. Details: the assigned handlers patch removes foreign-pane ownership probing from Stop (new lines 865-906), all tmux attach setup (1696-1966), and tmux resize operations (2076-2084). The shipped retirement premise is the same commit's service/core/old_terminals implementation and startup integration, specified in SPEC_impl.md lines 2891-2929: startup ends the old server and reload gives old-kind rows no terminal. Could-be-highest: yes, this terminates user-owned processes and discards terminal state. Suggested bucket: highest (loss of work), retained for the parent's independent specification-acceptance check. Confidence: confirmed source/contract analysis; no execution. proposed_drop: explicit specification acceptance only, not rarity or lack of impact. Exact acceptance, SPEC.md at this commit, Terminal experience, lines 3006-3007: 'This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' Lines 3008-3010 retain ended-agent outcomes but discard their screens and close old tabs; lines 3014-3016 also explicitly accept a cleanup failure allowing Restart beside an old surviving agent. SPEC_impl.md lines 2210-2235 limit the terminal switch points to host runtimes and grid attaches. possible_cover: parent supplied likely analogous records g099/g113/g118/g130; no coverage sources searched and no duplicate disposition asserted. Caveats: the retirement is deliberate per the quoted contract, so this record asks for independent acceptance verification, not a behavior reversal; startup retirement's correctness is outside this handlers group. Prior candidate classification was insufficient and is superseded by this finding revision under the same ID. No parent drop accepted.

event.summary: Joining displaced grid senders under the attachment mutex does not wait on that mutex
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the new sequential cleanup loop initially looked capable of stalling all terminal attachments during takeover, but the replacement sender has a cancellation branch that does not acquire the attachment mutex. Details: handlers.rs lines 1865-1886 request shutdown of every displaced sender before awaiting any join. service/grid_stream.rs lines 937-963 select shutdown.changed() before the stream future and invoke report_forwarder_end synchronously after it. The sender holds no external process. service/terminals.rs lines 478-482 await only that task and log join errors. Source refutation: unlike the removed tmux forwarder, there is no external control client or reaping barrier to wait for here. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; the considered effect was cross-session terminal responsiveness (high if established). Suggested bucket: other, not reportable. Confidence: confirmed from source; no execution. proposed_drop: false positive refuted by the sender shutdown path; its reporting caller is checked separately below before closing the pass. possible_cover: none. Caveat: no claim about panic recovery beyond the removed external-resource barrier, or unrelated grid input behavior.

event.summary: Joining displaced grid senders under the attachment mutex does not wait on that mutex
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the cleanup loop's considered cross-session terminal-unresponsiveness consequence is refuted by the sender shutdown path. Details retained: handlers.rs 1865-1886 requests shutdown of all displaced output tasks before joining; grid_stream.rs 937-963 races shutdown before streaming and reports synchronously; connection.rs 1272-1328 dispatches Requested as a no-op and delegates natural-detach work. No output task waits for attachments, and no external tmux control-client reap remains. Suggested bucket: other, not reportable for this considered deadlock. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route for this output-join suspicion. Confidence: confirmed source analysis, no execution. proposed_drop: false positive refuted by the sender shutdown and verdict-dispatch paths; unchanged basis, no parent disposition assumed. possible_cover: none for the considered deadlock. Discovery-turn interface synthesis: g124/l1 is a DISTINCT input-lifetime finding, not refuted by c2. Pinned connection.rs 1510-1516 keeps partially moved old.input alive past drop(attachments), whereas HostAttach::drop at grid_stream.rs 1169-1175 sends pump cancellation. Its original potential-highest stale-input/command-mixing consequence remains owned by g124/l1, including the accepted-API versus bundled-GUI dimension-trigger caveat supplied by that group. This group checked its corresponding paths: handlers.rs 1877-1886 scopes each partial old to the for iteration, so old.input drops before replacement installation at 1956 and map unlock at 1968; explicit handle_detach scopes a to the if block at 2000-2006 before the outer attachment guard drops at 2007. Thus these handler scopes do not reproduce the newly reported cancellation-after-map-unlock interval. This does not prove cancellation preempts an already-polled pump, does not claim runtime-accepted input is revoked, and does not lower or drop g124/l1. Caveat: the candidate resolves only the original output-join concern; the natural-detach interface finding and the separately supplied already-polled handover issue retain independent provenance.

event.summary: Stop comment overstates the full-screen final-frame rule
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: an internal comment says a stopped full-screen program's last frame is not retained, although a terminal host can keep that frame; this does not establish incorrect user-visible behavior. Details: the changed comment at handlers.rs lines 945-948 attributes a blanket non-retention rule to SPEC.md. SPEC.md Terminal experience, lines 2895-2899, distinguishes programs that leave their alternate screen on exit from ones killed without doing so, whose frame remains in the same terminal. SPEC_impl.md Launch failure classification, lines 2703-2708, says the supervisor must take no snapshot before stopping and must paint none into a restarted terminal, while the host keeps its last screen. The executable handler agrees: it takes no snapshot, leaves the host and attachment intact, and at lines 1144-1150 explicitly says the host keeps the final screen. Could-be-highest: no; no source route from this comment to lost work or security impact. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed documentation discrepancy, source-only. proposed_drop: narrow internal-comment discrepancy with no established behavior defect; do not treat it as a failure to retain a stopped terminal. possible_cover: none. Caveat: the useful part of the comment, that Stop does not capture and store a frame, remains correct.

event.summary: Stop comment incorrectly says full-screen final frames are never retained
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the internal explanation of Stop tells future developers that a full-screen program's final frame must not remain after exit, although the product deliberately keeps it when the program does not leave its alternate screen. Details: changed handlers.rs lines 945-948 say SPEC.md states 'a full-screen program’s last frame is not retained after it exits and no snapshot of it is taken or stored.' The first half is false for the host-only terminal model this patch introduces. SPEC.md Terminal experience, lines 2897-2901, explicitly says a program that does not leave its full-screen display, 'because it was killed, say', leaves that frame showing in the same terminal and keeps it across supervisor restarts. SPEC_impl.md Launch failure classification, lines 2703-2708, distinguishes retaining the original terminal from taking a snapshot and painting it into a restarted terminal. The executable handler does not capture a snapshot and correctly leaves the original host and attachment intact; lines 1144-1150 even explain that the host keeps the final screen. The concrete misinformation is a nonexistent blanket ban on retaining the existing terminal's last frame, which could misdirect lifecycle maintenance or tests toward clearing a frame the product promises to keep. Suggested bucket: other (documentation correctness). Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route from this comment. Confidence: confirmed source/contract discrepancy; no execution. proposed_drop: false; lack of an executable behavior defect does not refute this bounded documentation issue. possible_cover: parent supplied g117c3 as an analogous stale lifecycle explanation; no coverage sources searched and no duplicate disposition asserted. Caveats: this is not a claim that stopped frames currently disappear, and the comment's separate rule against taking/storing a pre-stop snapshot remains correct. This finding revision supersedes the prior proposed drop under the same ID; no parent drop accepted.

event.summary: Listing error comments falsely claim unreadable launch sentinels fail the request
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: developers are told a session-list request can fail because a launch-sentinel file cannot be read, although launch-file failures are deliberately handled by the background ticker and leave listings available. This misstates the error boundary and can steer a failure fixture or maintenance change toward the wrong operation. Details: assigned handlers.rs 620-622 rewrites list_reply's testability explanation to say a genuinely failing listing takes an unreadable launch sentinel or checkout registry. Lines 653-657 repeat the sentinel as a request-fatal failure and cite list_all's documentation as justification. The bounded full list_all source at service/listing.rs 88-153 directly contradicts this: its contract at 90-93 states 'Lists never sample screens, apply reports, read launch artifacts or commit outcomes' and 'A launch artifact read failure leaves lists available; the ticker logs and retries it.' Its complete function snapshots and projects entries; the sole fallible await is store.project_checkout_metadata at 139, and it performs no launch-file observation. entry_info is the previously checked synchronous retained-state projection. Suggested bucket: other (internal error-contract documentation). Could-be-highest: no established or suspected security or user-work-loss route from this comment. Confidence: confirmed pinned source/contract discrepancy; no execution. proposed_drop: false; correct listing behavior is not a refutation of the distinct documentation defect. possible_cover: none in the supplied neighbour records for this specific error-boundary claim; no prohibited coverage search. Caveats: checkout metadata failures can genuinely fail a listing, so the whole comment need not disappear; replace the fictitious sentinel example and align its rationale with the actual checkout projection. The parent revision's list_all already separates ticker-owned launch evidence, so history of the stale sentinel claim across the full pinned range is being checked before final attribution; this finding does not yet claim the assigned commit first introduced the stale clause.
